baseline_definition: The historical standalone evidence baseline measures progress toward four self-contained field units that do not depend on a phone, server, or repeater; it is retained for continuity and is not the current V1 Companion release total.

baseline_milestones.name: Architecture and safety contracts
baseline_milestones.description: Protocol, recovery, privacy, group-size, and degraded-operation rules are documented and extensively host tested.
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Close remaining product-firmware architecture gates with target evidence.

baseline_milestones.name: Core OpenTrail firmware
baseline_milestones.description: Hardware-neutral communication, status, alert, persistence, update, and recovery components plus a portable-client composition exist; real board bindings remain.
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Bind the selected client hardware and prove the complete target composition.

baseline_milestones.name: Firmware loading app
baseline_milestones.description: A packaged Windows inspection shell identifies the three bench runtimes, presents non-authoritative vendor-family hardware candidates with explicit maintenance steps, and verifies bounded bundle structure, image SHA-256, and RSA-PSS-3072/SHA-256 when a signer is pinned; production trust, authoritative board matching, writing, and recovery remain absent.
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Run separately authorized maintenance probes for received-board evidence, obtain independent trust review, and approve signer custody plus pinned production trust before implementing any writer.

baseline_milestones.name: Heltec V4 bench firmware
baseline_milestones.description: Two assembled Heltec V4 units retain bounded historical MeshCore bench evidence. OT-DEV-001 is an experimental OpenTrail target with exact-profile build, physical boot/BLE advertisement, and startup/status OLED evidence. OT-083 and OT-084 reject both on-chip authorization rollback-floor candidates, so Decision 0028 defers protected ownership/control beyond the current Heltec V1 rather than weakening it. OT-085A installed and verified the exact OT-085 image, accepted one fixed privacy-safe public BLE read, and physically observed `BLE CONNECTED` followed by the phone-disconnect return to `BLE ADVERTISING`. OT-085B accepted target-initiated automatic termination inside the bounded interval, the same owner-observed display lifecycle, and return of exactly one compatible service advertiser without claiming stable identity; every protected characteristic, claim, and command remains closed. The exact installed partition/source proof, private OT-064 recovery application, recovery contracts, and dormant protected-root foundations remain accepted historical evidence without current runtime authority.
baseline_milestones.evidence_status: Experimental physical target with bounded public BLE link
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Continue bounded non-privileged target integration; protected authorization remains deferred to future hardware.

baseline_milestones.name: Firmware for the first complete unit
baseline_milestones.description: The display, internal radio/GNSS module, power path, enclosure, and exact production target still require a frozen build and integration.
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Freeze the exact hardware and complete one recoverable end-to-end client.

baseline_milestones.name: Four-person V1 field proof
baseline_milestones.description: Four identical standalone clients must pass recovery, range, endurance, usability, and repeatable field trials before V1.
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Run the frozen four-unit standalone pilot and accept its evidence.

release_tracks.name: V1 Companion
release_tracks.definition: A complete V1 Companion release means four Trail Essential device-and-Android-phone pairs can be installed, privately authorized, used for direct group communication and location awareness, recovered, and field tested without depending on a server or internet connection.
release_tracks.rounding_rule: Calculate the exact weighted result, then round to the nearest whole percentage for public display.

milestones.next_gate: Close remaining product-firmware architecture gates with target evidence.

milestones.next_gate: Bind the accepted security, radio, GNSS, and persistence components into the selected Companion target.

milestones.name: Firmware loading app
milestones.description: The shared desktop loader provides bounded offline inspection, while production trust, authoritative board matching, writing, and recovery remain absent.
milestones.next_gate: Accept production signing and board authority, then prove bounded writing, verification, and recovery.

milestones.name: Heltec V4 / Trail Essential target
milestones.description: One experimental target has exact-profile build, physical boot, startup/status OLED, heartbeat, privacy-safe BLE-advertisement evidence, a bounded physical partition/source proof, a privately retained OT-064 recovery application, and accepted recovery/protected-root contracts. Both on-chip authorization-floor candidates are rejected, and Decision 0028 defers protected ownership/control beyond current Heltec V1 rather than weakening it. OT-085A installed and verified the exact OT-085 image, accepted one fixed public BLE read, and physically observed the phone-disconnect connected-to-advertising lifecycle. OT-085B accepted target-initiated automatic termination inside the bounded interval, the same owner-observed display lifecycle, and return of exactly one compatible service advertiser without claiming stable identity; all protected characteristics, claims, and commands remain closed.
milestones.evidence_status: Experimental physical target with bounded public BLE link
milestones.next_gate: Continue bounded non-privileged target integration; protected authorization remains deferred to future hardware.

milestones.name: Android companion application
milestones.description: Three of five equal evidence gates are accepted: build/install/lifecycle/artwork acceptance, exact-service discovery, and bounded physical public GATT connection/read evidence covering both phone-disconnect and target-initiated automatic disconnect/re-advertise lifecycles. OT-086 accepts the plan-only OTAR0/v0 operational-release contract. OT-087 freezes version 1/1.0.0 and accepts an explicit non-debuggable unsigned release-build foundation plus packaged inspection. OT-088 freezes the private-pilot privacy/data-safety, first-release rollback/removal, and bounded support policies. Five of eight plan prerequisites are satisfied; physical matrix, release identity, and signer/custody remain blocked. No signed, installed, supported, distributed, production-ready, or operationally accepted candidate exists. Protected authorization remains deferred on current Heltec hardware.
milestones.evidence_status: Build tested with bounded physical public BLE read, unsigned release-build foundation, and accepted private-pilot policy foundation
milestones.next_gate: Satisfy physical matrix, release-identity, and signer/custody prerequisites, then execute the accepted OTAR0/v0 private-sideload-v1-pilot plan as one coherent release-candidate evidence set; keep protected one-phone authorization and Ready deferred pending future hardware.

milestones.name: Four-person Companion field proof
milestones.description: Four frozen Trail Essential and supported Android pairs must pass recovery, range, endurance, usability, and repeatable field trials before V1 Companion.
milestones.next_gate: Approve the Companion pilot amendment, freeze four device-phone pairs, and run the accepted field sequence.

change_log.reason: Established the first evidence-weighted V1 Companion baseline. Shared architecture, core firmware, loader, and Heltec evidence are counted once; Android receives two of five equal gates for physical install/lifecycle/artwork and exact-service discovery, while live GATT, protected authorization and Ready, operational release acceptance, and four-person field proof remain open.
Recorded one consumed, sanitized OT-DEV-001 source-read denial and owner-observed startup/status return. Source proof remains absent, so no milestone completion changed.

Accepted the exact installed partition-table and complete blank protected-storage source-region proof on OT-DEV-001, followed by the owner-observed startup/status return. This satisfies only the source prerequisite, so no milestone completion changed.
Accepted a private exact capture of the installed OT-064 application as recovery input. The recovery route and every transition authority remain open, so no milestone completion changed.

Accepted the exact source-restore route, expected disabled security-state preflight, post-first-write recovery-uncertain policy, and protected-key/rollback-floor requirements offline. Physical recovery, concrete providers, fresh unified evidence, and every transition authority remain open, so no milestone completion changed.

Selected the two protected-key provider roles and a conditional custom user-eFuse thermometer floor class offline. Exact physical allocations, inventory, provisioning, recovery, fresh unified evidence, and every transition authority remain open, so no milestone completion changed.

Accepted the offline protected-root inventory plan and pure supplied-evidence verifier. At OT-079 acceptance no complete inventory reader/orchestrator existed, no device inventory or allocation was observed, and every physical, provisioning, runtime, and transition authority remained closed, so no milestone completion changed.

Rejected unsafe host-side eFuse materialization and accepted only a pure target-side decoded-metadata interface contract. No adapter, device read, floor descriptor, allocation, provisioning, or runtime authority exists, so no milestone completion changed.

Accepted the build-only six-slot coarse key-roster adapter after strict host/static checks, the complete host gate, and two identical pinned target builds. It has no runtime call path, was not device-executed, and cannot prove complete inventory or provider suitability, so no milestone completion changed.

Accepted the build-only default NVS-configuration and decoded security-state source after strict host/static checks, the complete 145-executable host gate, and two identical pinned target builds. It has no runtime call path, was not device-executed, and cannot prove current device state, complete inventory, or provider suitability, so no milestone completion changed.

Rejected the conditional custom USER_DATA eFuse rollback-floor candidate after pinned ESP-IDF evidence proved its Reed-Solomon coding unit cannot support repeated independent writes. The two protected HMAC roles remain selected by type, but no viable floor provider is selected and no device or runtime changed, so no milestone completion changed.

Rejected ESP32-S3 SECURE_VERSION as the independent companion-authorization floor after pinned ESP-IDF evidence proved its 16-step firmware anti-rollback role and OTA-only native model conflict with the accepted factory recovery route. External monotonic hardware remains a future hardware-revision option with no part selected, and no device or runtime changed, so no milestone completion changed.

Deferred rollback-protected companion authorization beyond current Heltec V1 and accepted the OT-085 build-only fixed public BLE read plus bounded link/display lifecycle after the complete 148-executable native host gate, eleven target-admission groups, and two identical pinned target builds. The image was not flashed, no physical connection/read/display transition occurred, and all protected control remains closed, so no milestone completion changed.

Accepted one OT-085A physical public GATT connection/read and phone-disconnect return to advertising on the exact verified OT-085 image. The owner observed BLE CONNECTED followed by BLE ADVERTISING, and the sanitized phone harness rediscovered the same in-memory endpoint without retaining identity. This closes the third of five equal Android evidence gates and advances that milestone from 40% to 60%; the Heltec milestone completion remains 25% because no separate scoring increment is defined. Protected authorization, Ready, the independent 15-second termination path, operational release, and field evidence remain open.

Accepted OT-085B physical target-initiated automatic BLE termination on the exact verified OT-085 image. The Android 13 harness made no disconnect request, accepted the successful remote disconnect inside the target-derived bounded interval, and observed exactly one compatible service advertiser return; the owner observed BLE CONNECTED followed by BLE ADVERTISING. This closes the automatic-termination sub-gate but defines no separate scoring increment, so the Heltec milestone remains 25% and Android remains 60%. Protected authorization, Ready, operational release, and field evidence remain open.

Accepted the plan-only OTAR0/v0 Android operational-release contract, canonical private-sideload-v1-pilot plan, and fail-closed admission validator with execution blocked. No production candidate, signing, installation, supported-device, operational, support, distribution, or release evidence was added, so Android remains 60% and V1 Companion remains exact 43.75% / displayed 44%.

Accepted the OT-087 Android unsigned release-build foundation at version code/name 1 / 1.0.0 after debug/release tests, lint, assembly, and packaged artifact inspection. This satisfies exactly the production-variant and stable-version plan prerequisites, while physical matrix, privacy/data-safety, release identity, rollback, signer/custody, and support remain blocked. No signing, installation, phone/device, account/store, distribution, or operational-release acceptance occurred, so Android remains 60% and V1 Companion remains exact 43.75% / displayed 44%.

Accepted the OT-088 private-pilot privacy/data-safety, first-release rollback/removal, and bounded best-effort/no-SLA support policies without executing them. Five of eight OTAR prerequisites are satisfied; physical matrix, release identity, and signer/custody remain blocked. No phone, installation, signing, account, upload, distribution, support delivery, or operational-release acceptance occurred, so Android remains 60% and V1 Companion remains exact 43.75% / displayed 44%.
